solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Language Sean misused in jest

indicators.note: the jumbled name sits inside the word for a jest

parts.note: a jape is a joke or jest

indicators.note: letters that are misused are put to the wrong use, so the name is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone mangles a language for comic effect, with poor Sean's name misapplied in a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Language' heads the clue, and the surface hides it as the subject of the sentence rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese is the national tongue spoken in Japan.

clue.text: Dog equipment in outskirts of arena

indicators.note: the gear goes inside those two edge letters
the outskirts are the outer edges, so only the first and last letters of the word are used

parts.note: kit is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: A dog's gear is laid out round the edge of a show arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' arena leaves A...A, and KIT goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Akita is a large spitz-type breed originally from northern Japan.

clue.text: Nocturnal tree-dwelling lemur half visible, certainly

indicators.note: only half of the animal's name can be seen, so just its first half is kept

parts.note: a nocturnal lemur of Madagascar

explanation.surface: A wildlife spotter is sure they glimpsed half of a lemur up a tree at night.
explanation.walkthrough: The aye-aye's name is a doubled word, so half of it is simply AYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aye is an old or dialect word of assent, meaning yes, surely.

clue.text: Record old companion's age

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone documents how old their long-time friend is.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is a Companion of Honour, a UK award given for service to the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long historical period or era.

clue.text: German city engineer's inner nature

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr region of Germany
CE is short for civil engineer

explanation.surface: A German city's engineer shows his true character.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence is the intrinsic quality that makes a thing what it is, its core character.

clue.text: Fraud unknown on south-west island

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: SW is the compass abbreviation for south-west
algebra uses letters like Z for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: An unidentified swindle is going on at an island off the south-west coast.
explanation.walkthrough: A swiz is informal British slang for a swindle or a disappointing letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiz, a British colloquial word, means a cheat or swindle, so a fraud.

clue.text: Romantic musician, seconds before, excited Andre

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so the name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A romantic singer gets Andre worked up seconds before he performs.
explanation.walkthrough: ERE is an old poetic word for before, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenader sings or plays love songs beneath a sweetheart's window.

clue.text: Church worker in Ireland chilled drink

indicators.note: the church and worker pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for Ireland

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a worker bee; in crosswords worker often means bee or ant

explanation.surface: A church employee in Ireland enjoys a cold drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice beer is a lager brewed by partly freezing it, served very cold.

clue.text: Dull English or US coin

parts.note: dim means dull, of light or of wits

explanation.surface: A dreary choice between English money and an American coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is the American ten-cent piece.

clue.text: Someone who looks old alongside British waiter

parts.note: a server waits at table

explanation.surface: An elderly customer watches a British waiter at work.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer is a watcher or onlooker who notices things.

clue.text: Damage new hat on long-distance race

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage

indicators.note: the letters are made new, put in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A runner ruins a brand new hat while pounding out a long race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like an adjective for the hat, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a road race of about 26 miles.

clue.text: A Greek character joins blokes in scheduled recreation

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the men go inside the word for scheduled

parts.note: set as in fixed or arranged in advance
blokes are men

explanation.surface: A Greek joins some lads for planned leisure time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scheduled' gives SET in the sense of fixed in advance, as a set time.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement means entertainment or pastime, a way of enjoying oneself.

clue.text: Want Geordie to meet newsman

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle, in the North East (NE) of England
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A Tynesider wishes to be introduced to a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to want or require it.

clue.text: Untidy person's thorough wash mostly very loud

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a scrub is a vigorous wash
FF is fortissimo, the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A grubby individual's good scrub is noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of SCRUB to leave SCRU.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruff is a shabby, dishevelled individual.

clue.text: Conversation starts to echo around Una's French country house

parts.note: a chat is an informal conversation

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words means their initial letters

explanation.surface: Talk begins to echo through Una's grand house in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes E, A and U from echo, around and Una's.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or large manor in the countryside.

clue.text: Cool weapon for group of admirers

parts.note: to fan is to cool by moving air
a club is a blunt weapon

explanation.surface: A chilled-out weapon somehow becomes a body of supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan club is an organised society of devotees of a celebrity or team.

clue.text: Stop by English river last

parts.note: an end is a stop or finish
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone halts beside an English river for the final time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like an adjective tacked on, but it is the verb meaning to persist.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to persist or go on lasting over time.

clue.text: Lie in hospital, exhausted

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters across the next two words

explanation.surface: A worn-out patient rests in a hospital bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' reads as resting, but it is the noun for an untruth, and the letters sit in hospiTAL Exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale can mean a falsehood, as in telling tales.

clue.text: In New York, university cream broadcast skill in maths

indicators.note: the other pieces go inside the abbreviation for New York
broadcast seed is scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A New York college puts out ads for cream, plus a lesson in arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges CREAM into MERAC; with U it goes 'In' NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Numeracy is competence with numbers, the arithmetic counterpart of literacy.

clue.text: City chief recalled legendary Rovers footballer, American

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Roy Race, hero of the British comic strip Roy of the Rovers

explanation.surface: A civic leader remembers a famous American player for Rovers.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy of the Rovers was a long-running British football comic; 'recalled' turns ROYAM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the elected head of a city council.

clue.text: Gracious female, upper-class, somewhere in the Ionian Islands

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'gracious!'
U denotes upper-class usage in British slang

explanation.surface: A refined, well-born lady lives on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gracious' reads as an adjective for the lady, but it is the exclamation COR.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is one of the Greek islands in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Live empty life in same Yorkshire town

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: the emptied word goes inside the word for same

parts.note: very as in 'the very same'

indicators.note: an empty word has its middle removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone leads a hollow, unchanging existence in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' life leaves LE, which goes 'in' VERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Beverley is a market town in the East Riding of Yorkshire, famed for its minster.

clue.text: Father and son rage

parts.note: S is a genealogical abbreviation for son
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: A parent and child both lose their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To sire is to beget offspring; as a noun it means a male parent, especially of an animal.

clue.text: Visit Ely perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to call on them
second meaning: Ely, a Cambridgeshire cathedral city

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a sightseeing tip; a see is the diocese a bishop governs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to go and meet someone and is also the seat of a bishop's authority.

clue.text: Resign from actor's union without case

indicators.note: the case is the outer shell, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: Equity is the trade union for actors in the UK

explanation.surface: A performer leaves their union after losing a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the British performers' union; stripping its case removes E and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a post or body is to leave it, to step down from it.

clue.text: Wine Rob tipped over — "oops" heard

indicators.note: tipped over means upended, so the name is read backwards
heard says the exclamation is spoken and spelt to fit

parts.note: d'oh is Homer Simpson's 'oops' of annoyance

explanation.surface: Rob knocks over the claret and someone cries 'oops!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped over' makes ROB into BOR; DEAUX sounds like 'd'oh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux is a French wine from the region around Bordeaux, often red claret.
